newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power output falls 2.8 pct vs. year-ago - EEI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power output falls 2.8 pct vs. year-ago - EEI.

text.p: The electricity deliveries in the continental U.S. totaled 70,395 gigawatt hours (GWh) for the week ended Aug 31, down 2.8 percent from the same period in 1995, the Edison Electric Institute (EEI) said Thursday.
The amount of power supplied last week to the Midcontinent U.S. fell sharply due to more seasonal summer temperatures compared with near record heat in the region last year.

EEI said the South Central region, which includes Texas, Louisiana, western Mississippi, southeastern New Mexico and most of Arkansas and Oklahoma, showed the largest decline last week, down 13.1 percent at 9,571 GWh.
Electric output in the 48 contiguous states for the latest week fell 5.1 percent from the previous week.
Year-to-date domestic power production totaled 2.25 million GWh, up 2.1 percent from the comparable period in 1995, EEI said.
